metadata.context: Latency, accuracy, use cases, and robustness of pipelines for understanding dynamic environments in shared autonomy for power wheelchairs on edge hardware (Jetson Orin Nano)
metadata.threshold: total_score >= 14 OR high relevance (>=4) unique in niche

shortlist.title: Real-time open-vocabulary perception for mobile robots on edge devices: a systematic analysis of the accuracy-latency trade-off
shortlist.abstract: Systematic analysis of optimization trade-offs for real-time open-vocabulary robotic perception on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB, evaluating combinations of NanoOWL and YOLO-World detection models paired with NanoSAM and EfficientViT-SAM segmentation models, optimized via TensorRT at FP32, FP16, and INT8 precision. Best pipeline (NanoOWL FP16 + EfficientViT-SAM-L0) achieves 47.51 FPS with 84.64% mIoU on RefCOCO+. Provides practical guidance for deploying Vision-Language Models on Jetson Orin for human-robot interaction.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The only paper in the set that directly benchmarks open-vocabulary perception pipelines on Jetson Orin-class hardware with end-to-end latency numbers. It evaluates TensorRT precision trade-offs (FP32/FP16/INT8) with quantitative mIoU and FPS, making it uniquely actionable for Jetson Orin Nano deployment decisions. The RefCOCO+ evaluation and real-time threshold (>10 FPS) align directly with wheelchair navigation requirements for dynamic scene understanding.

shortlist.title: FAST-LIO2: Fast Direct LiDAR-inertial Odometry
shortlist.abstract: Efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry system that registers raw point clouds directly to maps without feature extraction and employs an incremental k-d tree (ikd-Tree) for dynamic map maintenance. Operates at up to 100 Hz and supports multiple LiDAR types. Achieves consistently higher accuracy at lower computational load than competing systems, benchmarked across 19 sequences from multiple LiDAR datasets. Compatible with both Intel and ARM-based processors.
shortlist.evaluator_note: FAST-LIO2 is a high-impact LiDAR-inertial odometry system widely adopted as a backbone for mobile robot localization in dynamic environments. Explicit 100 Hz operation, ARM processor compatibility, and open-source availability make it directly relevant to Jetson Orin Nano deployment. The 19-sequence multi-dataset benchmark provides strong rigor, and its feature-free registration approach reduces compute overhead critical for edge systems.

shortlist.title: NGD-SLAM: Towards Real-Time Dynamic SLAM without GPU
shortlist.abstract: CPU-exclusive visual SLAM system for dynamic environments that decouples camera tracking from deep learning-based masking via a mask propagation mechanism and employs a hybrid tracking strategy combining ORB features with optical flow. Achieves 60 FPS tracking on a laptop CPU while maintaining high localization accuracy in dynamic environments. First SLAM system to demonstrate feasibility of deep learning for dynamic SLAM without GPU support.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Uniquely addresses the GPU-free constraint directly applicable to scenarios where the Jetson Orin Nano GPU must be reserved for perception inference. Demonstrating 60 FPS SLAM on a CPU-only platform with dynamic object masking is highly relevant to shared autonomy wheelchairs. The hybrid ORB + optical flow tracking improves robustness in crowded, dynamic environments. Open-source code availability supports reproducibility.

shortlist.title: PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds
shortlist.abstract: PointPillars encodes point clouds organized into vertical columns (pillars) via PointNets, enabling fast and accurate 3D object detection at 62 Hz (105 Hz for faster variant) for autonomous driving. Outperforms all prior methods on KITTI 3D and bird's eye view benchmarks including fusion-based approaches using only LiDAR. Designed for computational efficiency with a lean downstream 2D convolutional detection network.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Seminal paper establishing the pillar-based point cloud encoding paradigm that achieves real-time LiDAR detection (62-105 Hz). Its 2D convolutional backbone is highly compatible with TensorRT/edge deployment on Jetson hardware. The KITTI benchmark rigor and wide adoption across downstream robotics systems make it an essential reference for any LiDAR-based dynamic obstacle detection pipeline. Frequently used as backbone in wheelchair and mobile robot systems.

shortlist.title: LV-DOT: LiDAR-visual dynamic obstacle detection and tracking for autonomous robot navigation
shortlist.abstract: LiDAR-camera fusion framework integrating outputs from multiple low-accuracy but computationally efficient detectors to avoid demands of sophisticated 3D detection systems for indoor robot navigation. Employs tracking via feature-based association and Kalman filtering with a dynamic obstacle classification algorithm. Validated on datasets and physical quadcopter experiments, outperforming benchmarks across IoU thresholds.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Most directly applicable recent paper to the wheelchair use case: explicitly targets indoor robot navigation under compute constraints, uses lightweight multi-detector fusion instead of heavyweight 3D networks, and validates on physical hardware. The LiDAR-camera fusion with Kalman filtering mirrors the sensor configuration typical of smart wheelchairs. High relevance score (5) as it covers dynamic obstacle detection in shared indoor spaces with edge constraints.

shortlist.title: Deep Person Detection in 2D Range Data
shortlist.abstract: Extends the DROW wheelchair and walker detector to general person detection using 2D laser range data from mobile robots, incorporating temporal information through a short online window in the network architecture. Creates the largest dataset of person annotations in 2D range data from real-world environments. Demonstrates superior performance over three baseline methods, addressing occlusion, dynamic leg motion, and crowding.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Uniquely relevant as it originates from wheelchair/walker detection (DROW dataset) and extends to general person detection in crowded spaces — precisely the dynamic obstacle type encountered by power wheelchairs in indoor environments. The robustness evaluation explicitly covers occlusion, leg motion dynamics, and crowding. 2D LiDAR is a lower-compute alternative to 3D LiDAR well-suited for edge deployment, making this a niche-specific essential reference.

shortlist.title: Deep Learning-Based Object Detection, Localisation and Tracking for Smart Wheelchair Healthcare Mobility
shortlist.venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
shortlist.abstract: Perception system for autonomous wheelchairs adapting YOLOv3 for object detection with Intel RealSense depth estimation and SORT-based tracking for indoor navigation objects (doors, door handles). Achieves 90% door detection precision and 3.8% mean depth estimation error. Pipeline runs at 5.8 FPS on Jetson TX2 embedded hardware and 30 FPS on desktop GPU, validated in a controlled lab with Vicon motion capture ground truth.
shortlist.evaluator_note: The only paper in the set validated directly on a wheelchair platform with embedded GPU hardware (Jetson TX2), providing concrete FPS benchmarks (5.8 FPS embedded vs 30 FPS desktop) that establish a performance baseline for edge deployment. The SORT tracking integration, RGB-D depth pipeline, and healthcare mobility context make this the most application-specific paper in the set. Essential reference for Jetson-based wheelchair perception system design.

shortlist.title: LeGO-LOAM: Lightweight and Ground-Optimized Lidar Odometry and Mapping on Variable Terrain
shortlist.abstract: Lightweight and ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping method for real-time six-DOF pose estimation with ground vehicles, using point cloud segmentation to filter noise and feature extraction for planar and edge features. Two-step Levenberg-Marquardt optimization achieves real-time pose estimation on low-power embedded systems, demonstrating similar or better accuracy than LOAM with reduced computational expense on variable terrain.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Seminal lightweight LiDAR SLAM system explicitly designed and validated on low-power embedded hardware for ground vehicles — the closest analogue to wheelchair platforms among SLAM papers. The ground-plane optimization is relevant to wheelchair navigation where the robot operates near floor level. Its widespread adoption as an edge-deployable SLAM backbone in assistive robotics makes it an essential baseline reference.

shortlist.title: Simple Online and Realtime Tracking with a Deep Association Metric
shortlist.venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP 2017)
shortlist.abstract: Extends the SORT tracking framework by incorporating deep appearance features learned offline on a large-scale re-identification dataset, using nearest neighbor queries in visual feature space for measurement-to-track association. Reduces identity switches by 45% while maintaining real-time performance by offloading complexity to offline pre-training. Enables tracking through longer periods of occlusions.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Seminal multi-object tracking algorithm widely adopted as the detection-to-tracking bridge in robotics perception pipelines, including the lecrosnier_2020 wheelchair paper. The 45% reduction in identity switches under occlusion directly addresses the crowded indoor environment challenge. Real-time tracking with offline-trained appearance features is well-suited to edge deployment where training compute is separate from inference. Essential methodology reference for dynamic obstacle tracking.

shortlist.title: Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments Using Context-Aware Human Trajectory Prediction
shortlist.abstract: Integrates context-aware human trajectory prediction combining intention recognition with trajectory optimization-based motion planning into a full robot perception and motion planning framework, validated on a Toyota Human Support Robot using live RGB-D camera data. GPU-accelerated predicted composite distance fields significantly reduce computation time. Releases the Oxford Indoor Human Motion dataset for indoor human trajectory research.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Only paper in the set that closes the loop from dynamic environment understanding through to robot motion planning in human-shared indoor spaces, validated on a real assistive robot (Toyota HSR) with live sensor data. The context-aware trajectory prediction with intention recognition is directly applicable to shared autonomy wheelchairs navigating among pedestrians. Releases a novel indoor human motion dataset, adding research infrastructure value.

shortlist.title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation
shortlist.abstract: Unifies camera and LiDAR data in a shared bird's-eye view space preserving both geometric and semantic information for multi-task multi-sensor perception. Achieves a 40x reduction in view transformation latency through optimized BEV pooling and sets new state-of-the-art on nuScenes for 3D detection and BEV map segmentation. Supports multiple 3D perception tasks with minimal architectural modifications.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Strong sensor fusion baseline with a 40x latency reduction in the BEV transformation stage — a critical bottleneck for multi-modal perception pipelines. While primarily targeting autonomous driving rather than assistive robotics, BEVFusion's unified BEV representation is increasingly adopted for indoor robot perception. The MIT-Han Lab affiliation and ICRA 2023 venue ensure high rigor and downstream impact on edge-optimized perception systems.

shortlist.title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking
shortlist.abstract: Represents 3D objects as points and detects centers using keypoint detection, then regresses 3D dimensions, orientation, and velocity, simplifying tracking to greedy closest-point matching. Achieves 65.5 NDS and 63.8 AMOTA on nuScenes and outperforms previous lidar-only methods on Waymo Open Dataset. Second-stage refinement uses additional point features to improve estimates.
shortlist.evaluator_note: CenterPoint unifies 3D detection and tracking into a single elegant framework by representing objects as center points, achieving CVPR 2021 state-of-the-art on both nuScenes and Waymo. The joint detection-tracking formulation is highly relevant to dynamic environment understanding pipelines where tracking latency matters. Its simplicity (greedy matching rather than graph association) makes it a strong candidate for edge-adapted implementations.

shortlist.title: Moving Object Segmentation in Point Cloud Data using Hidden Markov Models
shortlist.venue: IROS 2024 Workshop on Long-Term Perception for Autonomy in Dynamic Human-shared Environments
shortlist.abstract: Learning-free method using hidden Markov models to segment dynamic objects in point cloud data, modeling individual voxels with HMMs and integrating probabilistic beliefs into maps through HMM filtering. Performs competitively with deep learning approaches on benchmark datasets while maintaining strong generalization across different sensor types and environments. Publicly available code.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Uniquely valuable as a learning-free alternative to deep learning MOS approaches, offering strong cross-sensor generalization without retraining — critical for edge deployment scenarios where the target sensor may differ from training data. The IROS 2024 workshop venue ('Long-Term Perception in Dynamic Human-shared Environments') directly matches the wheelchair context. High robustness score reflects demonstrated generalization across sensor types and environments.

shortlist.title: CoNav Chair: Design of a ROS-based Smart Wheelchair for Shared Control Navigation in the Built Environment
shortlist.abstract: ROS-based smart wheelchair platform using a shared control navigation algorithm and obstacle avoidance to support people with disabilities while maintaining user autonomy in indoor social environments. Emphasizes trust and autonomy for acceptance of assistive mobility technologies in the built environment, bridging the gap between full autonomy and manual control. Provides a reference architecture for wheelchair shared autonomy systems.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Directly addresses the shared autonomy wheelchair use case in indoor social environments — the most application-specific match to the research context. Provides a reference ROS architecture with obstacle avoidance for power wheelchairs, grounding the literature review in a concrete system design. While quantitative performance details are sparse in the preprint, its deployment focus (indoor built environment) and use case alignment (relevance=5) justify inclusion as a use-case anchor paper.

shortlist.title: Receding Moving Object Segmentation in 3D LiDAR Data Using Sparse 4D Convolutions
shortlist.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) / IROS 2022
shortlist.abstract: Converts sequential LiDAR scans into sparse 4D voxel representations and applies computationally efficient sparse convolutions to extract spatiotemporal features, predicting per-point moving object confidence scores. A receding horizon strategy enables online predictions with a binary Bayes filter for robust estimation. Evaluated on SemanticKITTI and Apollo datasets using only geometric information without semantic labels.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Strong methodological contribution for LiDAR-based moving object segmentation using sparse 4D convolutions that are more computationally efficient than dense alternatives. The geometric-only approach (no semantic labels required) improves generalization — important for wheelchair environments where semantic training data for all obstacle types is unavailable. Cross-domain evaluation on Apollo demonstrates robustness across datasets, a key concern for deployment.

shortlist.title: Moving Object Segmentation in 3D LiDAR Data: A Learning-based Approach Exploiting Sequential Data
shortlist.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) / IROS 2021
shortlist.abstract: LMNet uses sequential range image representations from rotating 3D LiDAR with CNNs to distinguish moving from static objects, operating faster than sensor frame rate in urban settings. Introduces a new evaluation benchmark derived from SemanticKITTI for LiDAR-based moving object segmentation. Benchmark and code released publicly.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Foundational paper establishing the LiDAR moving object segmentation (LiDAR-MOS) benchmark on SemanticKITTI that subsequent papers (mersch_2022, sun_2022) use as their evaluation standard. The range image CNN approach is computationally lighter than 3D voxel methods, making it more feasible for edge hardware. Essential as the benchmark-setting paper for the LiDAR-MOS task relevant to dynamic obstacle detection for wheelchairs.

shortlist.title: DynaSLAM: Tracking, Mapping and Inpainting in Dynamic Scenes
shortlist.abstract: Builds upon ORB-SLAM2 to add dynamic object detection and background inpainting, operating across monocular, stereo, and RGB-D configurations. Detects moving objects through multi-view geometry, deep learning, or both, and uses a static scene map to restore frame backgrounds occluded by dynamic objects. Outperforms standard visual SLAM in highly dynamic environments.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Seminal paper establishing dynamic visual SLAM as a field, widely cited as the baseline for subsequent dynamic SLAM work. Its RGB-D configuration matches the sensor modality used in many wheelchair systems (e.g., Intel RealSense). The multi-strategy dynamic detection (geometry + deep learning) provides a methodological template for hybrid approaches. High robustness score reflects evaluation across multiple SLAM scenarios with moving people.

shortlist.title: Social LSTM: Human Trajectory Prediction in Crowded Spaces
shortlist.abstract: Data-driven LSTM model with a novel social pooling layer that pools hidden representations from neighboring agents' LSTMs to capture human-human interactions for trajectory forecasting in crowded settings. Demonstrates improvements over traditional social force models, learning behaviors including collision avoidance and group movement. Achieves more than 42% improvement over previous methods.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Seminal paper establishing the data-driven approach to pedestrian trajectory prediction in crowded spaces — directly applicable to wheelchair navigation among people. The social pooling mechanism to model pedestrian interactions is foundational to all subsequent trajectory prediction work (SocialGAN, AgentFormer). While not edge-optimized, its CVPR 2016 publication and 42%+ accuracy improvement make it a canonical reference that any dynamic environment understanding review must include.

shortlist.title: BEVFusion: A Simple and Robust LiDAR-Camera Fusion Framework
shortlist.abstract: Addresses LiDAR-camera fusion framework limitations when LiDAR malfunctions by processing camera features independently, enabling robust detection under sensor failures. Outperforms state-of-the-art by 15.7% to 28.9% mAP under simulated LiDAR malfunction conditions. First method to handle realistic LiDAR malfunction without post-processing.
shortlist.evaluator_note: Highest robustness score (5/5) in the set for explicitly testing under simulated sensor failure conditions — a critical concern for assistive robotics where sensor reliability directly affects user safety. The 15.7-28.9% mAP improvement under LiDAR malfunction provides quantified evidence of robustness that other fusion papers lack. Relevant to wheelchair systems where both cameras and LiDAR may be disrupted by environmental conditions.

excluded.reason: Borderline score (16/25) but superseded by mersch_2022_4dmos in the shortlist with similar total score. MotionSeg3D contributes dual-branch spatial-temporal fusion — the core methodological distinction (motion-guided attention modules) is captured in the mersch paper discussion. Including both would be redundant for a 12-18 paper target. Score: rigor=4, relevance=4, latency=3, robustness=3, edge=2, total=16.

Score 13/25, below threshold. The paper addresses dynamic object removal for urban outdoor navigation, but lacks detail on latency, specific datasets, or hardware evaluation. The scan-to-map / map-to-map framework is relevant but insufficiently differentiated from other dynamic SLAM approaches already in the shortlist.

Score 12/25, below threshold. DynaSLAM II extends DynaSLAM I (bescos_2018, which is included as seminal) with tightly-coupled MOT but provides no latency metrics, no hardware evaluation, and the abstract notes code was not yet released at submission time. Lower rigor than the original and not uniquely differentiated from bescos_2018_dynaslam already in the shortlist.

Score 14/25, at minimum threshold. Scene flow estimation is a related but distinct task from dynamic obstacle detection — it estimates motion vectors rather than classifying moving objects. The paper's primary contribution is a new large-scale dataset; the FastFlow3D model is not benchmarked on edge hardware. Marginally relevant to the wheelchair pipeline and excluded to stay within the 18-paper target.

Score 11/25, below threshold. Occupancy flow fields for motion forecasting are relevant conceptually but the paper is evaluated on autonomous driving data (INTERACTION dataset) with no latency reporting, no edge evaluation, and no indoor/assistive robotics context. The speculative occluded agent prediction is interesting but not validated for the target deployment scenario.

Score 14/25, at minimum threshold but excluded in favor of alahi_2016_sociallstm (seminal) and yuan_2021_agentformer (more recent Transformer approach). Social GAN sits between these two methodologically and adds the GAN training paradigm, but without latency or edge evaluation it does not add unique value to the shortlist beyond what the seminal LSTM and modern Transformer papers cover.

Score 14/25, at minimum threshold. AgentFormer is a strong trajectory prediction paper but focuses on Transformer-based sociotemporal modeling for autonomous driving benchmarks without any real-time latency analysis, edge deployment evaluation, or indoor/assistive robotics validation. The agent-aware attention mechanism is notable but not sufficiently grounded in the target deployment context to include over papers with higher edge relevance.
